THE TRACE FORENSIC LAB

Every click leaves a trace.
What will you do with it?

Step into a fictional investigation. Preserve the evidence, test your assumptions, and explain what you find.

Begin your first investigationNo live systems. No real personal data.
Learn by making decisions
LAB 01

Your first digital crime scene

A laptop, a suspicious invoice, and a running system. Make five decisions that determine whether your evidence survives scrutiny.

Evidence handlingChain of custodyDecision-making
20 min Unit 2Enter lab
LAB 02

One bit. A different story.

Hash a fictional invoice, change a single character, and see why integrity verification is indispensable. All calculations happen in your browser.

SHA-256Integrity verificationDisk imaging
12 min Unit 4Enter lab
LAB 03

The account behind the account

Work with a completely fictional public-profile dataset. Link an alias to an organization while separating observation, inference, and identity.

OSINTSource evaluationAttribution
18 min Unit 3Enter lab
LAB 04

A signal in the noise

Inspect synthetic network events, distinguish routine updates from suspicious periodic connections, and build a cautious investigative hypothesis.

Network forensicsTraffic analysisTimeline reconstruction
15 min Unit 3Enter lab
LAB 05

The invoice that wasn’t

An accounts employee receives a changed bank account instruction. Examine the headers and payment clues before deciding what to preserve.

Email headersPhishingFraud triage
15 min Unit 1Enter lab
LAB 06

Make your evidence court-ready

Prepare Part A and Part B of a fictional electronic-evidence certificate. Understand the source, lawful control, device particulars, hash, and signatories.

BSA section 63CertificationEvidence presentation
18 min Unit 2Enter lab
LAB 07

Can you trust the alert?

Adjust a synthetic classifier’s decision threshold. Watch precision, recall, and false positives change, then decide how to triage alerts without treating a score as proof.

Machine learningPrecision & recallHuman review
15 min Unit 5Enter lab
These are educational simulations, not live forensic tools. Disk acquisition and OSINT use fictional scenarios; SHA-256 hashing is real and runs locally. Never practise on a real person or system without authority.
